children: NXP Semiconductors reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.786 billion, up 19% year over year, with GAAP diluted earnings per share of $3.48 and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $4.20. GAAP net income attributable to stockholders was $884 million. The company also announced a new $5 billion share repurchase authorization.
Revenue was $3.786 billion, up 19% year over year.
GAAP gross profit was $2.189 billion, with a 57.8% gross margin; non-GAAP gross profit was $2.217 billion, with a 58.6% margin.
GAAP operating income was $1.228 billion, with a 32.4% operating margin; non-GAAP operating income was $1.406 billion, with a 37.1% margin.
GAAP net income attributable to stockholders was $884 million.
Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share were $4.20; GAAP diluted earnings per share were $3.48.
Automotive, Industrial & IoT, and Communications Infrastructure & Other were the principal sources of year-over-year segment growth; Mobile revenue declined year over year.

NXP said accelerating contributions from automotive and industrial growth drivers and continued data center infrastructure momentum supported the quarter. It also cited software-defined vehicles and Trusted Physical AI as longer-term opportunities.
The BMW Group plans to deploy NXP’s Trimension ultra-wideband ranging and radar solutions across its fleet, beginning with selected 2026 vehicle programs.
NXP broke ground on an assembly and test site expansion in Malaysia, while VSMC, its joint venture with Vanguard International Semiconductor, opened its first 300mm fab in Singapore.
The board authorized a $5 billion share repurchase program, in addition to $1.3 billion remaining under the prior authorization.
